scope: Read rich files and scans. Use more document keys.

topics.title: Read rich files
details: The reader keeps headings, tables, lists, links, and bookmarks. Word files can show notes too. It reads DOCX, HTML, EPUB, ODT, Markdown, and data tables. Your source file stays as it was. Word files that the editor cannot keep now open for reading.
In the reader, H moves to the next heading. T moves to a table, K to a link, L to a list, B to a bookmark, and N to a note. Hold Shift to move back. Enter follows a link inside the file.

topics.title: Read scanned PDF pages offline
details: The app now uses a local AI engine to read text in scanned PDF pages. The models ship with the app. No page is sent to a web service. Pages with text keep their text. OCR is used for image pages with no text.
OCR can make errors. The reader reports lines with low scores. Check key facts in the source scan. A scan has no saved Word styles, so its old headings and tables may not be found.

topics.title: More document keys
details: Ctrl+Alt+1 through 6 sets a heading level. Ctrl+Shift+N sets normal text. Ctrl+Shift+L starts a bullet list. Ctrl+Shift+7 starts a number list. Ctrl+Alt+T asks for a table size.
Insert+F or Caps Lock+F says the format. Insert+Shift+Down or Caps Lock+Down reads the text you selected. Hold Insert or Caps Lock while you press the other key.
Every document menu action has a key or a short key sequence. Press Alt, a group number, then the item key shown in the menu.
